think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 15-year-old boy presents with an acute, painful, febrile eruption characterized by diffuse erythematous nodules, infiltrated plaques, a bullous leg lesion, hand abscess, and wrist swelling on top of a 1-year history of unnoticed distal sensory neuropathy. The tension lies in mistaking an acute severe systemic immune reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum) and superimposed bacterial abscess for an acute rheumatologic, streptococcal, or pyogenic condition rather than recognizing Hansen's disease.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint is reached when emergency physical examination (identifying characteristic facies, hypopigmented anesthetic macules, and thickened peripheral nerves), bedside ultrasound, and baseline hematologic/imaging workup are completed, immediately prior to obtaining diagnostic skin slit smears for acid-fast bacilli.
3. Differential Distinctions: Post-streptococcal erythema nodosum or reactive arthritis presents with tender subcutaneous pretibial nodules, fever, and arthralgias, but lacks diffuse infiltrated facial plaques, chronic sensory neuropathy, peripheral nerve trunk enlargement, madarosis, and saddle nose deformity. Severe pyogenic cellulitis/abscess can explain the swollen, tender forearm and leukocytosis, but cannot account for the diffuse symmetric nodular eruption and chronic hypoesthetic lesions. The confluence of bilateral ulnar/radial nerve hypertrophy, madarosis, saddle nose, and anesthetic macules confirms lepromatous leprosy undergoing a Type 2 lepra reaction.
case_prompt:
A 15-year-old immunocompetent male presents to the emergency room with a 2-week history of diffuse, non-pruritic cutaneous lesions, wrist joint swelling, chills, and acute exacerbation of numbness and tingling in his extremities. For the preceding year, he had experienced persistent sensory disturbances, numbness, and tingling sensations in his extremities without seeking medical care. On arrival, he is febrile and reports severe pain throughout his limbs. He denies gastrointestinal complaints, cough, dyspnea, chest pain, night sweats, or weight loss. He reports no personal history of allergies, recent sore throat, or similar illness among household contacts.

On physical examination, the patient appears acutely ill and in severe pain. Vital signs reveal a blood pressure of 100/60 mmHg, heart rate of 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute, and axillary temperature of 38.9°C. Conjunctival pallor is present. Dermatologic examination reveals multiple erythematous nodular lesions with poorly defined borders and infiltrated plaques distributed bilaterally across the face and hands. A non-blanching bullous lesion with a negative Nikolsky sign is present over the right leg. The left forearm is markedly swollen and tender to touch, displaying stretched, shiny overlying skin and a central blister. Neurologic and head-and-neck examinations demonstrate bilateral ulnar and radial cutaneous nerve enlargement, madarosis, saddle nose deformity, and tenderness over the olecranon. Cutaneous sensory testing reveals hypopigmented macules over the medial aspect of the left leg and bilateral thighs with distinctly decreased sensation.

Bedside hand ultrasound reveals a minimal superficial hypoechoic collection on the dorsal aspect (deepest pocket 0.4 cm) extending from the radial styloid to the fifth metacarpophalangeal joint, with increased subcutaneous thickness and echogenicity suggestive of an abscess. Complete blood count reveals microcytic hypochromic anemia with significant anisocytosis and neutrophilic leukocytosis with toxic granulation. Abdominal ultrasonography and plain chest radiographs are unremarkable.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Classic Erythema Nodosum / Post-Streptococcal Reactive Vasculitis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: While acute painful erythematous nodules, wrist swelling, and high fever resemble classical erythema nodosum, the absence of an antecedent streptococcal pharyngitis, the atypical distribution (face, hands, bullae), and the chronic one-year history of progressive peripheral nerve dysfunction rule out isolated reactive erythema nodosum.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: There was no history of allergy, recent sore throat, or similar illness in the household.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary Bacterial Cellulitis / Pyogenic Soft-Tissue Abscess
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Localized swelling, tenderness, and an ultrasound-confirmed superficial dorsal collection in the forearm indicated secondary pyogenic inflammation; however, isolated soft-tissue infection cannot account for the diffuse facial and bilateral hand plaques, bilateral cutaneous nerve enlargement, madarosis, and anesthetic skin patches.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: There were bilateral ulnar and radial cutaneous nerve enlargement, saddle nose, madarosis, and tenderness at the olecranon area (Figure 5).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The combination of bilateral enlarged peripheral nerve trunks, saddle nose, madarosis, and anesthetic hypopigmented plaques pointed to Hansen's disease, and a skin slit smear demonstrated abundant acid-fast bacilli, confirming lepromatous leprosy complicated by an acute Type 2 lepra reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum).
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The skin slit smear was taken for acid-fast bacilli, which turned positive for leprosy (Figures 6A,B).
